newsitem.title: CANADA: Union, GM talks stuck on overtime rules.
newsitem.headline: Union, GM talks stuck on overtime rules.

text.p: Talks between the Canadian Auto Workers union and General Motors Corp aimed at ending a strike by 26,000 Canadian auto workers are stuck over the union's refusal to accept mandatory overtime at GM's Oshawa factory, union and company sources said on Monday.
Both sides had cautioned earlier that disagreements over overtime rules at the Oshawa, Ontario plant, which employs some 13,000 of the striking workers, had the potential to derail the talks.

Nevertheless, negotiators said there was enough of an agreement on other crucial issues, such as outsourcing, to give them confidence that an overall deal could be reached in accordance with a labor agreement pattern that the union set in negotiations with Chrysler Corp last month.
"We have resolved the issue of outsourcing," union president Buzz Hargrove announced earlier on Monday.
Officials on both sides had expressed optimism that an agreement could be hammered out by an agreed 1200 EDT/1600 GMT deadline on Monday that would end the 18-day strike.

With that deadline now passed, GM and the union were still locked in tense negotiations in a downtown Toronto hotel, amid indications that the Oshawa Local 222, which represents workers at the sprawling complex, was holding out for a change in the mandatory overtime rule.
"They (GM) have just violated in every which way the spirit of that agreement," a union spokeswoman said.

Union officials said if they failed to reach a tentative agreement with GM today, the talks would probably be postponed until Thursday as pre-arranged union meetings precluded any continuation of the negotiations on Tuesday and Wednesday.
The strike, which has paralyzed all of GM's plants in Canada since midnight on October 2, has also idled 18,371 assembly line and plant workers in the United States and Mexico, GM said on Monday.

Shifts have been cancelled at four car assembly plants in the United States -- in Orion Township, Mich; Fairfax, Kansas; Wentzville, Mo. and Lansing, Mich. More than 2,000 workers are also now idle at GM's transmission plant in Warren, Mich and more than 1,000 at other plants in the state.
